Step 1. Purchase heavy-duty puncture-proof disposal bags (30 minutes)
Step 2. Research local hazardous waste disposal regulations (1 hour)
Step 3. Apply sealant to the base of the old wooden fence (2 hours)
Step 4. Transport collected scrap metal to the recycling center (1 hour)
Step 5. Buy a professional-grade soil testing kit (20 minutes)
Step 6. Backfill the hole left by the removed underground tank (4 hours)

Step 12. Dismantle the rusted, unstable swing set frame (3 hours)
Step 13. Inspect the yard for structural hazards and sharp debris (1 hour)
Step 14. Identify patches of invasive poisonous hemlock (30 minutes)

Step 30. Drain the remaining sludge from the underground tank (5 hours)

Step 33. Catalog all physical debris found during the sweep (1.5 hours)
Step 34. Conduct a final safety walkthrough of the cleared yard (1 hour)
Step 35. Gather scattered scrap metal into a central pile (3 hours)
Step 36. Hire a professional land surveyor (2 days)
Step 37. Pick up all visible shards of broken glass (4 hours)
Step 38. Scrub and sanitize the concrete patio surface (3 hours)
Step 39. Remove the decommissioned underground fuel tank (6 hours)
Step 40. Document the locations of all identified hazards (2 hours)
Step 41. Send soil samples to a laboratory for analysis (1 week)
Step 42. Order a large industrial dumpster for the renovation (30 minutes)
Step 43. Sweep the yard with a high-powered industrial magnet (2 hours)
Step 44. Bag up all loose insulation and asbestos-containing bits (5 hours)
Step 45. Take a photo of the cleared area for insurance records (15 minutes)
Step 46. Hire a pest control expert for a site inspection (1 hour)
Step 47. Stake out the "safe zones" for future landscaping (2 hours)
Step 48. Uproot the deep stumps of the hazardous trees (5 hours)

Step 50. Fill the excavation site with clean gravel (4 hours)
